title: Black queer men in Croydon | BLKOUT in Croydon
metaDescription: For Black queer men in and around Croydon: what's here, what's beside us, what's worth the journey — and a community-owned door into BLKOUT, the UK's co-operative for Black queer men.

landmark.alt: Pencil sketch of the Croydon Clocktower with the BLKOUT roundel as its clock face

hero.kicker: One community. Many doors. This one is Croydon's.
hero.heading: BLKOUT in Croydon
hero.standfirst: BLKOUT is a community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — and Croydon is our home borough. If you're a Black queer man in or near Croydon, you're not waiting for a community to arrive. You're already part of one. This page is the door.

quiz.heading: Know your Croydon?
quiz.sub: Three questions. No prizes except the stories.

questions.q: Ivor Cummings — the man BLKOUT carries the name of — was claimed as family by which Croydon household?

options.t: The family of composer Samuel Coleridge-Taylor
The Whitgift Foundation's board of governors
A Crystal Palace FC director's family

questions.reveal: Jessie Coleridge-Taylor, the composer's widow, sought out the Addiscombe schoolboy — a distant cousin through Sierra Leonean kinship — and claimed him. Three generations of Black British culture, one borough.

questions.q: In 1948, that same Croydon boy stood at Tilbury docks to do what?

options.t: Board the Empire Windrush for Kingston
Cover the arrival for the BBC

questions.reveal: Ivor Cummings — by then the openly gay civil servant historians call the gay father of the Windrush generation — met the ship and found the arrivals their first London beds.

questions.q: Which London borough is home to the largest Black population?
questions.reveal: Around 88,500 at the 2021 Census — and on any reasonable estimate, more Black queer men than anywhere else in the capital. You were never a niche.

scores.three: Croydon royalty. The borough should be asking you the questions.
scores.two: Nearly native. One night at the Ballroom should do it.
scores.low: All the more reason to walk through the door below.

here.heading: Here in Croydon
here.intro: BLKOUT is registered in Croydon, and our making programme is growing here — and the borough has a queer life of its own, with our people in it.

besideUs.intro: Croydon holds more queer life than the search results suggest. These neighbours do good work — use them, and tell them we sent you.

worthTheJourney.heading: Worth the journey
worthTheJourney.intro: Black queer men have never let a borough boundary decide where community happens — most of us travel for our people, and East Croydon puts the whole city within reach. Where you're centred, not just welcome:

entries.name: Black, Queer & Thriving — Black Thrive Lambeth
entries.note: Programmes and peer support for Black queer Lambeth — one stop up the line — including the Queer Minds peer group in Brixton.

entries.name: Melanin Vybz — London LGBTQ+ Community Centre
entries.note: Monthly group for LGBTQ+ Black people and people of colour over 50, at the Centre on Hopton Street, Southwark.

services.heading: Look after yourself
services.intro: Free, confidential, no GP needed, no judgement — and your business stays yours.

entries.name: Croydon Sexual Health
entries.note: The borough's free NHS clinic — STI testing and treatment, contraception, PrEP — and free self-test kits posted to any Croydon address. 530 London Road, CR7 7YE. (Croydon runs its own service; the London-wide SHL scheme doesn't cover this borough.)

entries.name: 56 Dean Street
entries.note: Soho's LGBTQ+ specialist sexual health and HIV service — Europe's largest, and long the home clinic of queer London.

entries.name: The Love Tank
entries.note: Community health action by and for us — the team behind PrEPster, directed by Marc Thompson of the Black and Gay, Back in the Day archive.

numbers.heading: The numbers nobody counts
numbers.body: The 2021 Census counted around 88,500 Black residents in Croydon — the largest Black population of any London borough, which on any reasonable estimate makes Croydon home to more Black queer men than anywhere else in the capital. The same census counted over 9,000 Croydon adults who identify as LGB+ — and more than 28,000 who preferred not to answer the question at all. The closet has a census line. These are working estimates and we welcome correction — but the point stands: we were never a niche. We were just never counted.
numbers.history:
Croydon holds three generations of Black British cultural life in one family story. Samuel Coleridge-Taylor, the borough's internationally celebrated composer; his widow Jessie, who sought out a Whitgift schoolboy — a distant cousin through Sierra Leonean kinship networks — and claimed him into the family; and that boy, Ivor Cummings of Addiscombe, who grew up to be the openly gay civil servant welcoming the Windrush generation ashore at Tilbury in 1948. The name over every BLKOUT door belongs to a Croydon son, claimed by a Croydon family.

The line continues: David McAlmont, one of the great British voices, is Croydon's too. The Museum of Croydon's BlackOut exhibition keeps the borough's Black queer story on record, and BLKOUT's own heritage project, Ivor's Compass, is part of the borough's Coleridge-Taylor 150 year. This door is that story in the present tense.

faq.q: Where can I meet other Black queer men in Croydon?
faq.a: Start with the door on this page — you'll hear about everything as it happens. Stanley Arts carries much of the borough's queer life including Ballroom, and BLKOUT's national community is open the moment you knock.

faq.q: Is there a Black queer night in Croydon?
faq.a: Stanley Arts in South Norwood hosts Ballroom — Black queer performance culture, in the borough. As more starts, it appears here first.

faq.q: Where can I get an STI test or PrEP in Croydon?
faq.a: Croydon Sexual Health at 530 London Road is free and confidential with PrEP available — and posts free self-test kits to any Croydon address. 56 Dean Street is thirty minutes up the line. No GP referral, no judgement.

BLKOUT is one community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — with a door in every borough. We're registered in Croydon, the borough our namesake grew up in, and we belong wherever our men are.

faq.q: I'm not out. Can I still come?
faq.a: Yes. Come as you are — nobody at this door asks you to be anything first, and your business stays yours.

truer.heading: Make it truer
truer.intro: This page got truer four times in one afternoon because one Croydon man read it. That's how it works: we check what we publish, and the borough corrects us. Know a night, a room, a group we've missed — or something here that's wrong or gone? Tell us. Corrections get credited, if you want the credit.
